## TL;DR

I walked every Settings tab (General, Notifications, Security, Advanced, Import/Export) and the Agents page's Budget Controls tab in headless WebKit at 375, 768 and 1280 px. None of them overflowed or threw page errors. The problems were accessibility: setting controls had no accessible name, because each row's label was a plain `div` with no link to its control. I fixed every instance the probe found, and the probe now passes 19 of 19 on two consecutive runs. Loading, empty and error states, and save-time validation messages were not covered.

## Work and rationale

Task #1263 asked for a sweep of layout, wording, save and validation on Settings General, the agents page and its budget tab, at three widths. The acceptance criteria require a headless walk, every issue fixed across its class, and a scoped check.

Budget Controls is a tab on the Agents page (`/agents?tab=budget-controls`), not a Settings tab, so I covered that route. The existing `agents-page-qa-browser.test.ts` (#1223) covers the other Agents tabs but not Budget Controls.

The first probe found five classes of issue, and the first handoff reviewer found more of the same:

1. Unnamed setting controls. Generic setting rows render `<div class="setting-label">` beside the control with no programmatic link, so switches, inputs and selects had no name. I added the row's label as `aria-label` at each config-driven row site in `SettingsView.vue`, and named each hand-written control.
2. Controls outside `SettingsView.vue`. Review found the same pattern in `ServiceSettings.vue`, `SettingsImportExport.vue`, `TelegramSettingsPanel.vue` (the test-message field) and `AuthSettingsPanel.vue` (the add-user email field). I named each one.
3. Focus. My first focus check read styles mid-transition, so inputs that use `transition-colors` looked unfocused. With transitions disabled in the probe, the shared `Input`, `Select` trigger and `Switch` all show a real focus change, so I left the shared primitives unchanged.
4. Probe false positives removed. Floating assistant buttons are named by their image `alt`, and the CTO checkboxes by their wrapping `<label>`. Radix's hidden native `<select aria-hidden>` elements are skipped. The probe now counts image alt text, label wrappers and `labels` as names.

I widened the probe from two pages to all five Settings tabs plus Budget Controls. When an unnamed control is found, the message now shows its type, name and placeholder, so the failing field can be identified from the output. The first all-tabs run listed the remaining instances, and each was fixed and re-run.

## Approaches tried

- A Tab-key walk. It is the most faithful focus test, but headless WebKit did not reliably give a fresh page keyboard focus. On some runs Tab went to the browser chrome and the walk saw zero controls. Retrying window focus did not fix it. I replaced it with an in-page audit that focuses each visible control in DOM order and compares its focused look with its resting look. It is deterministic, and it asserts that it reached at least one control.
- A string-injected in-page script. Playwright's `evaluate` accepts only self-contained functions, so the scripts became typed functions. The first build failed on that type error before any run.
- A stale bundle. The probe tests the built app. After an early source edit it reported old failures, so I rebuild after every source change.
- A malformed attribute. A script I wrote for the review fixes emitted a doubled quote (`:aria-label=""X""`), which broke the UI build. The build error caught it before any test ran. I repaired the attributes and rebuilt.

## Challenges and blockers

- Keyboard focus in headless WebKit is unreliable across pages. That is a limit of the probe, not a fix in the app. A real keyboard check would still be worth doing.
- The focus check confirms a focus change exists, not that it is visible enough. The `Input` and `Select` rings are a border-colour change (`--border` to `--border-bright`). I did not measure its contrast, so I cannot claim WCAG 3:1 for it.
- My first scoped check failed on `worktree-drift`. I had reverted an unused harness method while the check was running, so a tracked source file changed mid-run. The other steps passed. I re-ran the check with the tree left alone, and it passed every step.
- Shots. The review suggested declaring a route per walked page rather than the dashboard root. I declared two: `/settings?tab=general` and `/agents?tab=budget-controls`.
- Not covered: loading, empty and error states for these pages, and validation messages on save. The existing `settings-load-error` test passed, but I did not add fixtures for these two pages.

## Key learnings

- A visible label is not a name for assistive technology. A `div` next to a control needs an explicit name on the control, and `aria-label` from the same source string is the cheapest fix.
- Measure focus at rest. A colour transition makes a focus change look absent for about 150 ms, so the probe must disable transitions before reading styles.
- An audit that reaches nothing passes silently. The non-zero-stop guard is what made the empty walks visible.
- Widen the probe to the whole class, then let it list instances. Finding them by reading source would have missed AuthSettingsPanel and TelegramSettingsPanel.
